t:
The first paragraph of section 155 of title 18, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:

“Whoever, being a party in interest, whether as a debtor, creditor, receiver, trustee or representative of any of them, or attorney for any such party in interest, in any receivership, bankruptcy or reorganization proceeding in any United States court or under its supervision, enters into any agreement, express or implied, with another such party in interest or attorney for another such party in interest, for the purpose of fixing the fees or other compensation to be paid to any party in interest or to any attorney for any party in interest for services rendered in connection therewith, from the assets of the estate; or.”

fable.w: This section amends a criminal provision that prohibits fee-fixing agreements among private parties in bankruptcy, receivership, or reorganization proceedings. The words "agreement", "party in interest", and "proceeding" may suggest participation, but the agreement is among private parties and is the conduct being criminalized. No outside party is consulted on, or given a right to challenge, a federal decision.
fable.s: enters into any agreement, express or implied, with another such party in interest or attorney for another such party in interest, for the purpose of fixing the fees or other compensation

qwen_block.w: This section defines a criminal offense related to fee-fixing agreements among private parties (debtors, creditors, attorneys) in bankruptcy proceedings. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The interactions described are between private litigants, not between the government and the public.
qwen_block.s: Whoever, being a party in interest, whether as a debtor, creditor, receiver, trustee or representative of any of them, or attorney for any such party in interest, in any receivership, bankruptcy or reorganization proceeding in any United States court or under its supervision, enters into any agreement, express or implied, with another such party in interest or attorney for another such party in interest, for the purpose of fixing the fees or other compensation to be paid to any party in interest or to any attorney for any party in interest for services rendered in connection therewith, from the assets of the estate; or.

opus.w: This section defines a federal crime: private parties in a bankruptcy or receivership agreeing among themselves to fix fees. It does not set up any process where outsiders take part in a federal decision. The words 'party in interest,' 'agreement,' and 'court proceeding' look procedural, but the agreement is prohibited private conduct, not a consultation, hearing, advisory body, or right to challenge a federal decision.
opus.s: enters into any agreement, express or implied, with another such party in interest or attorney for another such party in interest, for the purpose of fixing the fees or other compensation to be paid
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the text mentions outside parties (debtors, creditors, trustees, attorneys), a "proceeding in any United States court," and an "agreement." That reading fails the definition. The provision is a criminal ban on private parties secretly agreeing among themselves to fix fees paid from a bankruptcy estate. No federal agency consults or coordinates with anyone outside the government before making a decision. Nothing creates a comment period, hearing or advisory body, and nothing gives outsiders a right to sue over a federal decision.
